text:
Anya: Heads-up — starting a 2-week "spring clean" to trim admin entitlements across infra projects. Goal: ~25% reduction where safe. Kicking off this thread for evidence collection, KMS grant checks, and rollback/runbook planning. Ping @Rahul for KMS mapping questions.

Rahul: Got it. Can you drop the owner map and current entitlement export? I have a small script to correlate KMS grants -> principals and last_use timestamps. Will run against staging first.

Marta: Quick question — are we pruning cross-account service grants in this pass? Dataflow and analytics teams rely on some of those and we should avoid surprise breakages.

Theo: Recommend we identify a critical-apps whitelist before any aggressive prune. Proposed minimal checklist per principal: owner confirmation, last-30d activity, key usage logs (KMS), role binding snapshot. Sample query I'll use: 
```
# pseudo-sql for owner/activity snapshot
SELECT principal, role, last_used, owner, project, kms_key_id
FROM entitlement_snapshot
WHERE role IN ('admin','owner')
ORDER BY last_used DESC;
```

Anya: Good call. Also add an "escape hatch" policy: any prune must include a 48h automated rollback window and a manual on-call escalation path. Put that in the runbook.

security-bot: Automated: access-review workflow created -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1427 :white_check_mark: (due in 14 days)

Rahul: Ran the mapping on staging this morning — found 12 KMS keys with cross-account grants, 3 ownerless service principals, and ~40 admin principals with no activity in 90d. Uploaded CSV to drive: https://drive.redwood/team-security/2026-03-admin-sweep.csv (raw).

Marta: I'll coordinate owner outreach for the flagged principals. For dataflow-critical keys we'll do a canary prune on the dev cluster + smoke tests before prod. Please tag the service teams in the CSV so they get email pings.

Theo: Proposed remediation cadence: small batches every 72 hours (to limit blast radius). Notify owners 72h before prune, run job to remove binding, monitor 24/72h, rollback if errors. Runbook snippet for rollback: 
* step 1: reapply previous binding via iam-restore job (idempotent)
* step 2: redeploy affected infra with --no-recreate flag
* step 3: escalate to on-call security if >2 failures

Anya: Assigning tasks: @Marta owners outreach + scheduling, @Rahul kms mapping + evidence artifacts, @Theo runbook + rollback automation, I'll compile the first-pass change set and post to eng-security for review before any changes.

Marta: One more note — audit logging retention gap: some audit logs older than 90d are already archived; attach retention proof when you send the change set so compliance can sign off.

Rahul: Acknowledged. I'll include KMS key policy diffs + CloudAudit snippets.

Anya: Perfect. Check-in mid-sprint on Friday. If anyone spots an urgent ownerless admin that looks risky, flag it here and we'll triage immediately. :thumbsup:

security-bot: Reminder scheduled: access-review reminder -> in 3 days.

Theo: Adding calendar invites for the first two prune windows and a quick canary dry-run on dev.

Anya: Thanks team — keeping this thread as the single source for artifacts + decision log.
